gloss: tea drinker; teetotaler; person who doesn't drink alcohol

definitions.gloss: tea drinker; teetotaler; person who doesn't drink alcohol
definitions.explanation: A person who prefers tea or other non-alcoholic beverages over alcohol. An older, somewhat playful expression contrasting with {左党|さとう} (a drinker). Derives from the traditional association of the right hand with rice (and by extension, non-alcoholic drinks).

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{右党|うとう}でお{酒|さけ}は{一切|いっさい}{飲|の}まない。
examples.english: My father is a teetotaler and doesn't drink alcohol at all.

examples.japanese: この{飲|の}み{会|かい}は{右党|うとう}にも{楽|たの}しめるメニューがある。
examples.english: This drinking party has a menu that non-drinkers can enjoy too.

examples.japanese: {左党|さとう}の{友人|ゆうじん}と{右党|うとう}の{私|わたし}では{飲|の}み{会|かい}の{楽|たの}しみ{方|かた}が{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: My friend who drinks and I who don't enjoy drinking parties in different ways.

notes:
The origin of this term relates to traditional Japanese customs. In the drinking culture, the {左|ひだり} (left) side was associated with sake (because craftsmen held their chisel in the left hand and their hammer — {槌|つち}, homophonous with a sake vessel — in the right), so {左党|さとう} came to mean a drinker. {右党|うとう} is its counterpart for non-drinkers.

This is an older expression that is still understood but less commonly used in modern casual conversation, where {下戸|げこ} (non-drinker) is more typical.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {右党|うとう}の{人|ひと}: a non-drinker
- {右党|うとう}も{左党|さとう}も: both drinkers and non-drinkers

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {左党|さとう}: drinker, sake lover — the opposite term for someone who enjoys alcohol
- {下戸|げこ}: non-drinker — the more common word for someone who can't or doesn't drink
- {上戸|じょうご}: heavy drinker — someone who can drink a lot
